newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends up, trade surplus news affects.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends up, trade surplus news affects.

text.p: The won ended firmer against the dollar on Tuesday as dollar sales continued despite fears of the central bank's dollar buying intervention, dealers said.
They said the release of a trade surplue in June raised expectations of dollar supplies, prompting dollar unwinding.
The won closed at a high of 887.80 against Monday's closing of 887.90. It opened at 888.00 and touched a low of 888.30.

"But no one dared to actively sell dollars due to the belief that the dollar would be supported at 887.50 level," a foreign bank dealer said. He forecast a trading range of 887.50 to 888.30 on Wednesday.
